decisions.diagnosis: The zero_outage trim cut the evening of the last good day before the outage, but the counter was still counting sparse late-night riders until 23:45.
decisions.evidence: After 20:30 the raw counts are 1,3,0,0,1,...,1,0,1 (North) and 3,0,0,1,1 (South), which fits normal late-evening traffic; restoring them gives complete days of 164 and 268 bikes. The outage of pure zeros starts on 2024-12-30.

decisions.diagnosis: The zero_outage trim cut the overnight hours of the first day back after the outage, but that morning's slots show the counter was already live.
decisions.evidence: There is 1 bike at 01:15 (North) and 2 at 05:00 (South), then normal dawn counts from 05:30; the raw totals are 98 and 152, in line with the days that follow (89-198 and 108-249).

summary: This is a single Metrocount piezo counter on The Strand at Dee Why with one record per slot and a plausible North/South split (South about 1.3-1.5 times North). It recorded pure zeros in both directions from 2024-12-30 to 2025-10-13 (288 days), which zero_outage already sets to missing, and the rest of the record has normal seasonal variation with no doubling or spikes. The only changes are to restore the few real night-time counts that the automatic trim removed on the two days at the edges of the outage.
